IG(S, A)= H(S) - Σ (|S_v|/|S|) H(S_v) for attribute A
Decision‑tree algorithm that selects splits by highest information gain
Estimate θ̂ = argmax_θ P(θ|D) = argmax_θ P(D|θ) P(θ)
Classifier assuming P(X|C)= Π_i P(x_i|C) for features x_i
Features x_i are independent given the class C
Chooses class with minimum expected loss under posterior distribution
Randomly selects a hypothesis from posterior and predicts with it
Directed acyclic graph representing joint distribution via conditional probabilities
Graph with directed edges and no cycles, used in belief networks
Classifies by majority vote of the k closest training points
Class chosen by the most frequent label among neighbours
Linear decision boundary defined by w·x + b = 0

takeaways: Decision trees split on attributes that give the highest information gain.
Bayes theorem updates prior belief with data likelihood to obtain a posterior.
Naive Bayes works well when feature independence roughly holds.
Support vector machines maximise the margin between classes for better generalisation.
Ensemble methods combine several weak learners to lower variance and bias.
k‑nearest neighbour relies on a suitable distance metric and choice of k.
bank_note: Syllabi stress clear definitions, derivations and comparative analysis of classifiers for long‑answer questions.

bank.q: Define entropy and compute the information gain for a binary split on a given attribute.
Explain Bayes theorem and illustrate how the MAP estimate differs from the maximum likelihood estimate.

glossary.def: Quantifies impurity or randomness in a set of class labels.
Reduction in entropy after splitting on an attribute.
Algorithm that builds a decision tree by greedy selection of highest information gain.
Formula to update probability of a hypothesis based on new evidence.
Initial belief about a hypothesis before seeing data.
Probability of observed data under a specific hypothesis.
Updated probability of a hypothesis after incorporating data.
Hypothesis with highest posterior probability.
Parameter values that maximise the probability of observed data.
Classifier that assumes conditional independence of features given the class.
Two variables are independent when a third variable is known.
Classifier that minimises expected loss under the posterior distribution.
Randomly picks a hypothesis from the posterior and uses it for prediction.
Graphical model representing joint probability via nodes and directed edges.
Graph with directed edges and no cycles, used to encode conditional dependencies.
Instance‑based classifier that predicts by majority vote of nearest training points.
Straight‑line distance between two points in Euclidean space.
Class label that appears most frequently among selected neighbours.
Flat subspace of one dimension less than the feature space; separates classes in linear models.
Shortest distance from the decision hyperplane to the nearest training sample.
Computes inner product in a transformed feature space without explicit transformation.
Ensemble technique that builds multiple models on bootstrap samples and averages their predictions.
Sequential ensemble method that focuses on previously mis‑classified examples.
Bagging of decision trees with random feature selection at each split.
Regression that fits a model using weighted nearby points, giving more influence to close data.
Kernel that depends only on distance from a centre, commonly Gaussian-shaped.
Solving new problems by adapting solutions of similar past cases.
